title: Vercel Says Jev Is Its Fastest-Adopted AI Model Ever, Reaching 35% of Paid Teams in Two Weeks
excerpt: TypeSafe AI's narrow decision model outran Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna on adoption while taking a sliver of spend — a sign of how quickly specialised models are becoming production infrastructure.
body:
• Jev, a lightweight "decision model" from TypeSafe AI, reached 35.3% of paid teams on Vercel's AI Gateway within two weeks of its September 17 gateway launch — the fastest adoption of any model in the platform's history, nearly double runner-up Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 18.1%.
  • Jev is built to choose between a few predetermined outputs, making each call faster and cheaper than a general language model; it took the most requests of any model in September while accounting for just 0.27% of gateway spend in its first two weeks.
  • Open-weight models now process 71.5% of gateway tokens and 23% of spend, up from one dollar in twenty in June; overall gateway spend in September was about 13 times December's, while the average price per token fell 47%.
  • Vercel itself uses Jev in production, having replaced GPT-6 Luna with it for classifying harmful commands.

The fastest-spreading AI model of the year is not a bigger chatbot. It is a small model that does one narrow thing — pick between a fixed set of outputs — and does it cheaply enough that a third of Vercel's paying teams wired it into production within a fortnight.

The numbers behind the claim

Vercel's October AI Gateway Production Index, published Thursday, ranks every September model launch by reach in its first two weeks. Jev, from TypeSafe AI, reached 35.3% of paid teams, against 18.1% for Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 and 14.9% for OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna. It also received more requests than any other model in September despite launching mid-month, and 55.6% of teams that tried it in week one came back in week two. The catch is scale: a Jev request uses a fraction of the tokens of a normal model call, so its record adoption translated into about 1% of September's tokens and 0.15% of spend.

https://x.com/vercel/status/2110803345309053144

Why a decision model spreads

As TechCrunch explains, constraining outputs is the whole design: classification, routing and moderation decisions do not need an open-ended essay, so a purpose-built model can answer faster and at a lower price than flagships such as Sonnet. Vercel is its own case study — it replaced GPT-6 Luna with Jev for classifying harmful commands. The buzz has already pulled competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon.

The market Jev landed in

The same index describes a market growing at both ends. September gateway spend was roughly 13 times December's; open-weight models took 71.5% of tokens and nearly a quarter of spend, with DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash alone processing close to half of all tokens for 2.6% of spend. Frontier spending grew tenfold even as its share shrank, and nearly one in three teams changed its most-used lab in a single month — an index record. Jev's rise fits that pattern precisely: models are becoming replaceable components, swapped per workload, and the cheapest adequate tool for a high-volume job wins fast. For the many Indian engineers building on Vercel and similar gateways, the practical takeaway is that model choice is now a cost line to be engineered, not a brand to be picked once.
